name: Facet
text: Make the graph’s nodes pulse once, bright and fast, when new data arrives. This keeps attention on freshness without overwhelming the screen. The trade-off is occasional distraction for users focused on static data, but it ensures no important update is missed.

name: Pane
text: The single bright pulse teaches users to wait for the next flash—like a stock ticker that trains attention on the wrong signal. A scaled pulse risks teaching users to ignore *all* pulses—just like a fire alarm that rings too often. Settle it by testing both against a static baseline: measure how long users take to notice real updates without training them to expect artificial urgency.
